_readme: Ramya's own authoritative professional profile. This file is the ONLY source opportunity_scoring.py and resume_tailoring.py may cite as fact. verified_experience is the only category resume_tailoring.py may present as fact in a draft. transferable_experience and knowledge_training may inform ramya_fit.gaps and framing language but are never rendered as hands-on fact. claims_requiring_verification are never used in any draft until moved to verified_experience by hand. First populated by Claude from real, founder-published content (aiforui.org's About page, sales-director/runtime/config/practitioner-bank.json) plus facts stated directly by Ramya, per AOS-PRACTICE-VALIDATION-ROADMAP.md's evidence discipline. Second-layer audited by Claude (Sept 2026): every VERIFIED claim re-checked against its cited source; every CLAIM_REQUIRES_VERIFICATION claim re-searched across the full repository for evidence missed the first time. One promotion resulted — 230+ vendors, corroborated by templates/proposals/third-party-risk-proposal-template.md and templates/proposals/dora-proposal-template.md, both real, founder-authored, client-facing content, independent of the About page. Everything else held at its prior classification because no new evidence was found; per the audit's own rule, absence of evidence is never treated as the claim being false, only as not-yet-usable. This is a DRAFT pending Ramya's own review before it is treated as canonical (see opportunity-intelligence-model.md's read-only rule) — nothing in Opportunity Intelligence has written or will write to this file; it is edited by hand only.

schema.verified_experience: array of {id, category, claim, employer_or_context, dates, tags, evidence_source, evidence_note} — category is one of: role, certification, project, skill, achievement. tags drive opportunity_scoring.py's tag-overlap matching. evidence_source is a precise pointer (repo file path or published URL); evidence_note is the narrative explanation. This is the only category resume_tailoring.py may present as fact.
schema.transferable_experience: array of {id, category, claim, context, dates, tags, evidence_source, evidence_note} — real experience in an adjacent area that supports but does not prove a specific target-domain claim; contributes to a fit score at a discounted (0.4x) weight, never as strong as a verified match
schema.knowledge_training: array of {id, category, claim, source, dates, tags, evidence_source, evidence_note} — training, certifications, frameworks studied, or self-study; tags are still recorded for gap-analysis visibility, but knowledge_training never contributes to an employment fit score (only verified_matches/transferable_matches do) — this is what keeps a certification from silently becoming an implementation claim
schema.claims_requiring_verification: array of {id, category, claim, evidence_source, note} — not found in any existing authoritative material as of the last audit; evidence_source is null unless a partial/insufficiently-precise source exists (see note). Excluded from every draft and from every score until Ramya confirms it and moves it to verified_experience by hand.
schema.target_professional_areas: array of strings — roles/domains Ramya is targeting, not a claim of experience in them. Descriptive only; not consumed by any scoring code.
schema.engagement_preferences: array of strings — format/geography/industry preferences, not qualifications. Descriptive only; not consumed by any scoring code.
schema.guardrails: array of strings — standing rules for anyone (human or future code) editing or extending this file. Not data to be matched against; a permanent reminder embedded in the file itself.

guardrails: Do not claim AI engineering, AI/ML development, or production AI model implementation unless authoritative evidence explicitly supports it.
Do not convert NIST AI RMF (or any framework) study/certification into implementation experience.
Do not convert framework knowledge into delivery experience.
Do not invent clients, projects, employers, certifications, metrics or outcomes.

Do not silently upgrade TRANSFERABLE or KNOWLEDGE into VERIFIED. Every promotion (see vendor-count-230-plus) must cite a specific, real, newly-found evidence_source, never a hunch that it 'sounds consistent'.
Do not treat 'not found in existing material' as 'the claim is false' — use CLAIM_REQUIRES_VERIFICATION, never silent deletion, for anything plausible but unconfirmed.

Do not manufacture precision — if a source says 'hundreds', the profile must not silently say a specific number unless a separate, real source establishes it (see vendor-count-230-plus vs. tprm-vendor-governance-lifecycle for the correct way to handle this).

Do not silently modify this founder-authoritative profile — every change is a human edit, reviewed before use; see opportunity-intelligence-model.md's read-only rule and its enforcing tests in tests/test_profile_is_read_only.py.

If a future capability proposes a change to this file, it must go through a separate proposal artifact and the approval_queue.py mechanism, exactly as documented in opportunity-intelligence-model.md — never a direct or automatic write.
